selected.title: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
selected.text: He also played a pivotal organisational, technical, and political role in India's Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998, the first since the original nuclear test by India in 1974.Kalam was elected as the 11th President of India in 2002 with the support of both the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party and the then-opposition Indian National Congress.

selected.title: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
selected.text: Widely referred to as the "People's President", he returned to his civilian life of education, writing and public service after a single term.

selected.title: Chittoor Mohammed Habeebullah
selected.text: A recipient of the Khwarizmi International Award in 1997, Habeebullah was honored by the Government of India, in 2001, with the fourth highest Indian civilian award of Padma Shri.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: Instituted in 1954, the award is conferred ``in recognition of exceptional service / performance of the highest order '', without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: The award was originally limited to achievements in the arts, literature, science, and public services, but the government expanded the criteria to include`` any field of human endeavour'' in December 2011.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: The recommendations for the Bharat Ratna are made by the Prime Minister to the President, with a maximum of three nominees being awarded per year.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: Recipients receive a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a peepal - leaf -- shaped medallion; there is no monetary grant associated with the award.

selected.title: Bharat Ratna
selected.text: Bharat Ratna recipients rank seventh in the Indian order of precedence.

selected.title: Lata Mangeshkar
selected.text: She is also the second vocalist, after M.S. Subbulakshmi, to have ever been awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian honour.

selected.title: Languages of India
selected.text: In addition, the Government of India has awarded the distinction of classical language to Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Sanskrit, Tamil and Telugu.
